name: Plunger lift and hydraulic jet pumps
aliases: Plunger lift and hydraulic jet pumps
principle: Plunger lift uses the well's own gas pressure to push a plunger and liquid slug up the tubing; hydraulic pumps (piston, jet) are driven by power fluid from the surface. Jet pumps tolerate solids above 50% by volume and hydraulic pumps cover about 1,000 to 18,000 ft.

process_steps.name: Gas pressure builds under the plunger
Well flows; plunger falls and cycle repeats

key_equipment: hydraulic jet pump and power-fluid system

source.note: Wikipedia, Artificial lift, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)
Wikipedia, Artificial lift, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.metric: plunger lift and hydraulic pump application envelopes (rate and depth)
performance.unit: blpd (hydraulic pump 25-4,000; plunger lift 1-100 vertical / 1-400 horizontal bbl per MMscfd gas, <5,000 ft TVD)
performance.basis: IPIECA Energy Efficiency Compendium artificial-lift table: plunger lift <5,000 ft TVD with liquid rate 1-100 (vertical) / 1-400 (horizontal) bbl per MMscfd of gas, no external power required except valve actuation; linear hydraulic pump 25-4,000 blpd, <15,000 ft TVD (jet/venturi pumps discussed under hydraulic pumping)

source.note: IPIECA Energy Efficiency Compendium, Artificial lift (2023), Table 1 (read 2026-10-28)

advantages: Plunger lift needs little surface equipment
limitations: The page gives no plunger-lift rate or depth figures
